regression.note: Five of six URLs are comparable to the 2026-07-30 audit. The service-area slot changed: the July audit used /service-areas/kenilworth-nj/, which now 301-redirects because the 2026-08-29 url-plan regeneration replaced it with a 52-area NJ/NY/PA set. This run audits /service-areas/union-nj/ (first area in the plan, no primary:true entry and no Kenilworth page remains), so that slot has no prior baseline. Prior per-URL lighthouse_issues arrays were capped at the top 5, so an issue absent from a prior list is not proof it was absent from that run; resolved_issues above are limited to ones confirmed by metric movement.

manual_findings.detail: JSON-LD LocalBusiness on all 6 pages still sets streetAddress '8 Harlow Crescent, Fair Lawn, NJ 07410'. The client record nap block says '500 S 31st St, Kenilworth, NJ 07033'. New this month: sameAs now lists BOTH cids (5612453956771500683 Fair Lawn and 8008820373441604497 Kenilworth), which is partial progress but leaves two GBPs claimed by one schema block. Also new: the service-area map iframe on /service-areas/union-nj/ embeds 'The Restoration Group Fair Lawn NJ', so a Union NJ page renders a Fair Lawn map.

manual_findings.title: Homepage meta description is 188 characters against the 70-160 target
manual_findings.detail: 188 chars: 'The Restoration Group provides 24/7 water, fire, mold and storm damage restoration across New Jersey, the NYC metro and eastern PA. Licensed, insured, IICRC-certified. Call (908) 970-8533.' Google will truncate around 160. The copy changed since July (Kenilworth to NJ/NYC/PA) but the length problem did not. This is the medium-severity issue that holds / at amber. DataForSEO has no description-length check id, so it is recorded here rather than as an onpage_issue.

verified_non_issues.note: DataForSEO reports has_micromarkup=false on all 6 pages. Manually verified that valid JSON-LD IS present on every page (Organization, WebSite, LocalBusiness, Service, FAQPage, BreadcrumbList). The check only detects microdata/RDFa, so this is a detection artifact and NOT a missing-schema finding.
Alt text coverage is 100 percent on all 6 pages (0 of 38 img tags missing or empty alt). The no_image_title flag is a separate, cosmetic title-attribute check and is not an accessibility requirement.

A raw scan for tel: hrefs surfaces the string 'tel:)' on every page. It is text inside a GA4 conversion-tracking JS comment ('every phone link (tel:) and form'), not a broken anchor. Every real anchor is tel:+19089708533.

instant_pages flags high_loading_time on /service-areas/union-nj/ (dom_complete 3991 ms). Lighthouse on the same URL returns performance 99, TTI 794 ms, LCP 804 ms. The gap is the lazy-loaded Google Maps iframe finishing after the user-visible render, so it is graded low and does not flip the page to amber.

No 4xx or 5xx outlinks, no mixed content, no meta-refresh redirects, no duplicate titles or meta tags, and exactly one H1 on all 6 pages. is_broken, is_4xx_code, is_5xx_code and https_to_http_links are all false.

environment_caveats: Lighthouse ran DESKTOP only (for_mobile=false, formFactor=desktop, cpuSlowdownMultiplier=1, throughputKbps=10240), matching the July baseline so the deltas are like-for-like. Mobile performance would typically score 10-20 points lower, and the homepage CLS regression would likely be worse on mobile where the hero copy wraps to more lines.

The dedicated on_page_lighthouse and on_page_instant_pages MCP wrappers were not exposed in this environment. The audit called the DataForSEO REST API directly (POST /v3/on_page/lighthouse/live/json and POST /v3/on_page/instant_pages) with the same parameters, and responses were written to disk before parsing.

Homepage was audited twice to test whether the CLS regression was run-to-run noise. Run 1: performance 92, CLS 0.15490. Run 2: performance 93, CLS 0.15490, identical layout-shift culprit node. The state file records run 1. CLS is reproducible to five decimal places, so the regression is real.
Audited the apex production origin. curl -sI returned no x-robots-tag noindex, so the SEO category counts toward every verdict and the staging-noindex correction does not apply.
Lighthouse 13.4.0 also returns an 'agentic-browsing' category (home 91, others 99-100). It is outside the four methodology categories and is excluded from scores, averages and verdicts.
